scope: Second-pass engineering and systems architecture audit of the ELV5 specification after the initial 8-finding discipline audit. This is design evidence only, not runtime acceptance.

findings.title: Engineering dimensions were exact numerically but not type-safe
findings.risk: dB/dBm, W/A/V, bit/s/bytes and other quantities could cross generic map/storage boundaries without a compile-time semantic barrier.
findings.resolution: Introduce code-owned dimension types, exact canonical units and typed Elv5Quantity wrappers shared by all 27 kernels.

findings.title: Canonical replay/input/output hash representation was underspecified
findings.risk: Semantically identical payloads could hash differently due to map order/number encoding, while volatile evaluation IDs/timestamps could destroy deterministic engineering output hashes.
findings.resolution: Freeze electra.canonical-json.v1 plus explicit request, input, output and snapshot hash projections; output hash excludes volatile record metadata.

findings.title: Engineering evidence basis and uncertainty were not first-class
findings.risk: Typical or estimated manufacturer/project values could accidentally satisfy checks that require guaranteed worst-case bounds; reserve could be confused with uncertainty.
findings.resolution: Add evidence basis, guaranteed intervals, applicability and conservative comparison semantics. Reserve is explicitly independent of evidence certainty.

findings.title: Operating-case and simultaneity identity was implicit
findings.risk: Expected/peak/startup/standby/alarm/emergency values could be combined across incompatible states or scenarios.
findings.resolution: Make operating case a captured input identity and require code-owned composition rules; process APIs bind state selections to the exact case.

findings.title: Schedule recurrence was not reproducible across timezone-rule changes
findings.risk: Host timezone or tzdb updates could alter storage/autonomy interval expansion and therefore engineering results or hashes.
findings.resolution: Pin IANA zone, tzdb version, DST gap/overlap policy and half-open UTC interval semantics in consumed evidence.

findings.title: Geometry frame identity and transform provenance were incomplete
findings.risk: Camera coordinates/rotations from different frames could be combined while still producing plausible numeric footprints.
findings.resolution: Introduce explicit frame identity, handedness, axis convention and transform-chain hash; mixed frames fail closed without captured transform evidence.

findings.title: All 27 processes lacked frozen process-specific Dart input/output boundaries
findings.risk: Generic maps could become de facto APIs and let different packages interpret the same process differently.
findings.resolution: Define typed process API shapes for CCTV-01..06, LAN-01..07, ACS-01..06 and FA-01..08, including shared typed header and output envelope.

findings.title: P2 storage roots and schema number were not concrete enough for implementation
findings.risk: Developers could normalize the same wire replacement command differently, choose incompatible root/child ownership, or duplicate existing command/history platforms.
findings.resolution: Freeze additive Drift schema 24, exact semantic tables/PK/FK/index rules, normalized roots/children, shared command ledger/history reuse and forbidden duplicate ownership tables.

findings.title: Multi-node publication atomicity was not explicit
findings.risk: A CALCULATE_DISCIPLINE_PROCESS batch could publish some nodes while another node fails captured-generation checks, yielding a mixed current workspace.
findings.resolution: Require all-or-nothing coherent batch publication with complete revalidation/CAS before any requested node becomes CURRENT.

findings.title: ACS emergency/fire/power-failure release semantics were too qualitative
findings.risk: Fail-safe/fail-secure behavior and emergency/fire release could be inferred from role presence or labels rather than an explicit expected-behavior matrix.
findings.resolution: Add lock safety mode and technical release truth table for normal access, request-to-exit, fire release, emergency break-glass and power-failure cases while preserving ELV7 compliance ownership.

findings.title: CCTV payload bitrate versus network wire-rate basis was not explicit
findings.risk: A payload/encoded bitrate could be compared directly with a physical link capacity without an explicit overhead/capacity model.
findings.resolution: Typed CCTV-02 API separates payload bitrate from optional versioned transport-overhead/wire-rate capacity evidence. No universal overhead percentage is allowed.

findings.title: Optical power budget could be overinterpreted as transmission reach
findings.risk: Passing Rx sensitivity/overload does not by itself prove dispersion/reach compatibility at a selected data rate.
findings.resolution: Keep power budget mandatory and expose reach compatibility only when an exact registered reach profile/model is available; otherwise no reach claim.

findings.title: Qualification strategy did not fully separate unit correctness from public vertical closure
findings.risk: Formula or structural registry tests could be mistaken for production command/persistence/concurrency acceptance.
findings.resolution: Define L0-L6 executable test layers, exact 54 POS/NEG primary verticals, adversarial 16-command matrix, restart/migration/failure/race tests, false-PASS sentinels and P9 exact-head evidence requirements.

findings.title: Scale behavior had no explicit qualification fixture
findings.risk: Correct algorithms could still enter runtime with pathological query/iteration behavior or SQLite batching limits.
findings.resolution: Add deterministic scale fixtures and benchmark evidence without inventing unmeasured production SLO thresholds.

deliberateStageBoundaries: ELV6 owns actual rack/cabinet slot, clearance, thermal and cable-management layout fit.
ELV7 owns verified jurisdictional/normative applicability and compliance certification.
ELV8 owns commercial product selection, BOM, quote and procurement deliverables.
ELV5 may preserve technical evidence useful to those stages but cannot silently claim their conclusions.
